ei.title: Shift in the Work-Time Paradigm Brought About by Industrialization

fullPassage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age ①<u>changed</u> the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine ②<u>what</u> runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand ③<u>to keep</u> the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and ④<u>production</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① changed: 과거시제 동사 — 적절.
✅ ② what: 선행사 A machine이 있으므로 관계대명사 that이 맞음. what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계사라 불가.
❌ ③ to keep: '~하기 위해'의 부사적 용법 to부정사 — 적절.
❌ ④ production: 명사로 effort와 병렬 — 적절.
det.tip: 관계대명사 what은 선행사 없이 단독으로 쓰이고, that은 선행사가 있을 때. 'a machine that runs'(돌아가는 기계).

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with ①<u>greater</u> speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is ②<u>dividing</u> into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you ③<u>made</u> ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became ④<u>clock-oriented</u>, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① greater: 비교급 형용사 — 적절.
✅ ② dividing: 근무일이 '나뉘는' 수동의 의미이므로 is divided가 맞음. 능동형 dividing 불가.
❌ ③ made: 과거시제, the more ... the more 구문의 병렬 — 적절.
❌ ④ clock-oriented: '시계 중심의'라는 형용사 — 적절.
det.tip: 수동태 be + p.p.: is divided(나뉘다). 능동형 ing는 주어가 '행하는' 경우에만.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, so that there ②<u>will</u> always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― ③<u>the more</u> hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started ④<u>reorganize</u> around new principles of productivity.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① one: a machine을 받는 부정대명사 — 적절.
❌ ② will: so that 구문에서 미래/의도를 나타냄 — 적절.
❌ ③ the more: 'the 비교급 ~, the 비교급 ~' 구문 — 적절.
✅ ④ reorganize: start는 to부정사나 동명사를 목적어로 취함. 동사원형 불가. started to reorganize가 맞음.
det.tip: start + to V / Ving. 동사원형만 단독으로는 목적어가 될 수 없음.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. As such, at many factories, the workday is divided into eight-hour shifts, ②<u>so that</u> there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ③<u>while</u> the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of ④<u>productivity</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① than: 비교급 more 뒤 than — 적절.
❌ ② so that: '~하도록' 목적의 접속사 — 적절.
✅ ③ while: 원문은 대시(―)로 삽입구를 연결. 'while'을 넣으면 'the 비교급 ~, the 비교급 ~' 구문이 종속절로 잘못 해석되어 주절과 호응이 깨짐.
❌ ④ productivity: 명사로 전치사 of의 목적어 — 적절.
det.tip: 원문의 대시(―)는 부연 삽입구를 이끈다. while로 바꾸면 문장 구조가 깨진다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ② value: 매 근무 시간의 '잠재 가치'를 끌어올렸다. 더 일할수록 더 벌게 된 맥락과 일치.
✅ ① danger: '위험'은 가치 상승 흐름과 무관.
❌ ③ silence: '침묵'은 본문 맥락과 전혀 맞지 않음.
❌ ④ boredom: '지루함'은 생산성 증대 맥락과 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: potential value(잠재 가치) - 실현 가능한 가치. 산업화로 시간 가치가 상승.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① volume: '더 큰 속도와 양' — 원문 그대로.
❌ ② shifts: 8시간 '교대' — 원문 그대로.
✅ ④ lowered: 원문은 raised(끌어올렸다). 더 많이 일할수록 더 많이 번다는 뒤 흐름과 정반대.
❌ ③ clock-oriented: 노동이 '시계 중심'이 되었다 — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: raised(끌어올렸다) ↔ lowered(낮췄다). 뒤 문장(the more ~, the more ~)이 가치 상승을 뒷받침.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 산업화가 시간을 노동의 가치 단위로 바꾸었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② made time the basic unit of labor's value: 시간당 생산량·임금이 산업화의 핵심 변화라는 본문 메시지.
❌ ① reduced the need for factory workers: 본문은 오히려 3교대로 사람을 계속 배치.
❌ ③ weakened the connection between wages and effort: 본문은 반대로 연결을 강화.
❌ ④ restored the traditional harvest-based lifestyle: 수확 기반 삶은 산업화로 대체된 과거임.
det.tip: 산업화 = 시간을 측정·보상 단위로 만든 사건.

det.korean: 사회 전반이 기계가 정한 시간 리듬에 맞춰 재조직되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ the entire society was reorganized around the time rhythm set by machines: 수확 주기에서 시계 중심으로의 전환과 '새로운 생산성 원리로 재편'이라는 본문 결론과 일치.

❌ ③ workers were allowed to work only when they wanted: 본문은 교대제로 강제 배치됨.

det.korean: ③ A machine what runs → A machine that runs.

questions.passage: The arrival of the Industrial Age changed the relationship among time, labor, and capital. Factories could produce around the clock, and they could do so with greater speed and volume than ever before. A machine that runs twelve hours a day will produce more widgets than one that runs for only eight hours per day ― and a machine that runs twenty-four hours per day will produce the most widgets of all. As such, at many factories, the workday is __________ into eight-hour shifts, so that there will always be people on hand to keep the widget machines humming. Industrialization raised the potential value of every single work hour ― the more hours you worked, the more widgets you produced, and the more money you made ― and thus wages became tied to effort and production. Labor, previously guided by harvest cycles, became clock-oriented, and society started to reorganize around new principles of productivity.
